final_rationale: The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence. The response usefully narrows the claim and concedes key limits, but that is reinterpretation of the same record, not closure of the initial audit concerns. The existing evidence can support the proposition that aggregate readiness passed and that disclosure of limitations is the policy-consistent path, but it does not show that the required disclosure has actually been made, that the limitation has been resolved, or that an approved mitigation or risk acceptance exists. Because those compliance predicates remain open on the present record, the verdict does not improve to compliant_with_caveats. The correct distinction is that a caveated theory may be plausible, but plausibility is not the same as evidentiary satisfaction of the policy conditions.
remaining_concerns: Admissible evidence still shows an unresolved weakness in a named launch use case: the HR benefits enrollment slice remains below target.
The mitigation artifact is still only a draft and still lacks a finalized owner and alert threshold; no approved mitigation with the required governance fields is in evidence.
The model-card draft still says there are no known material limitations, which remains in tension with the unresolved HR issue and reviewer comment.
The packet still supports, at most, a narrowed caveated position; it does not support a clean certification record or a no-limitations disclosure state.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance before launch or launch approval authorizing certification on this caveated basis.
